cards.title: The new rule from your A/B reason: R1.21, A recommendation is argued before it is asked
cards.context: Written from your three lines below, for book chapters only (not articles or letters). It sits after Turns and endings. Its 7 lines are numbered 1 to 7 below the notes.
said: it's just that the recommendation of pruning has not been argued or built up, or delivered powerfully
which are all a must for books that give a specific advice to follow
of course this problem is solved by length and thought, and storytelling sometimes and research, etc.
items: The goal: when a chapter asks the reader to do something specific, the reader is convinced before the ask, and the ask lands with force.
Build the case before the ask, over as many paragraphs as it needs: why the reader's way now fails them, and why this change is worth what it costs.
Each reason is argued, not named: it says why it holds and shows it in the reader's life. A reason given in one sentence and left is named, not argued.
The tools are length and thought, a story, another person's case or a study, each used where it fits. One story with an ask after it is not a case, however well told.
Thought works through what his material already holds. A reason the brain lacks is [MATERIAL NEEDED], never invented.
Deliver the ask plainly and with confidence: a concrete action, after the case is built.
The test: before the ask, point to each reason and its why. Fails: an ask that is only stated, an ask that rests on one story alone, or an ask whose case is squeezed into the last lines.
rows: Test
Your 14 test cases all come out right. But its checker passes both A/B drafts, X and Y, so it does not yet catch the problem you named. The section written again with the rule passes.
Wider wording

An earlier wording added four lines you did not say (why this change and not an easier one, name the reader's strongest doubt and answer it, deliver the ask once at the turn, a shrug test) and a strict checker note. It failed both A/B drafts in 3 runs of 3. A fresh review called it wider than your words.
Your scores
You scored the two drafts 7 and 8.25, not a fail.
options: a. Store this wording as Tier 1. It fails a draft that breaks it, but today its checker misses the A/B drafts.
b. Store this wording as Tier 2. The writer reads it on the chapter card. It never fails a draft, and no checker runs.
c. Store the wider wording as Tier 1. It catches both A/B drafts, but holds lines you did not say.
d. Store nothing yet. Wait until the next chapter shows the problem again, then word it from two cases.

cards.title: An API key for the checkers
rows: Now
The 20 checkers run as helpers inside the chat: about 1.5 to 2 million tokens of your plan for each final draft.
With a key
The same check is about 20 small API calls: about US$0.20 per draft on Sonnet 5.5, billed to the key.
Your steps if yes

Make a key in the Claude Console and add a little credit. Then add it to the cloud environment this project's chats use, under Environment variables, named CG_CHECK_API_KEY. Never name it ANTHROPIC_API_KEY there: Claude itself could pick that up and bill the whole chat to the key.
options: a. Get a key. Each check costs a little money and much less of your plan.
b. No key. Checks stay free beyond your plan and keep using its tokens.
